description:
FOUND s473t6c (#1501 ROUND 10), measured over the round's 90 t/op files.

PCL's `%Config` is a 108-key hand-written subset (`lib/Config.pm`) where perl's
is 1,253 keys on this machine.  A key perl always defines reads UNDEF here, so
a guard written against it takes the OTHER branch -- and because these guards
are usually `skip_all`, the file then produces NO ROWS AT ALL, which no bucket
but the shortfall can see.

MEASURED (probe `scratch/s473t6c/probes/config.pl`, perl | PCL):
    keys %Config        1253 | 108
    $Config{lseeksize}     8 | UNDEF
    $Config{sig_name}   same | same      (present)
    $Config{d_pipe}     same | same      (present)

THE SEVEN FILES IN THIS ROUND'S POPULATION that ask for a key PCL lacks:
    op/lfs.t        lseeksize                              <- 17 rows, the file
                    (`skip_all('no 64-bit file offsets')      SKIPS ITSELF
                      if $Config{lseeksize} < 8`)
    op/glob.t       usecrosscompile
    op/hexfp.t      d_long_double_style_ieee_extended
    op/inc.t        d_long_double_style_ieee_doubledouble
    op/infnan.t     usequadmath
    op/range.t      d_nv_preserves_uv
    op/sigdispatch.t d_sigprocmask

WHAT TO DO -- and what NOT to.  Adding a key is one line, but a key that turns
a `skip_all` OFF makes the file RUN, and a file that runs can add failing rows
and, in op/lfs.t's case, write multi-gigabyte sparse files.  So the fix is
per-key and measured: add the key WITH the value this machine's perl reports,
re-run the file `--jobs 1`, and read the rows before blessing anything.  The
honest general answer is to derive the whole table from the host perl's own
`%Config` at install time rather than to keep hand-listing keys -- that is the
decision this task carries (it also ends the drift: the current file's
`osvers` is a kernel string frozen in the repo).

Related: #1705 (a shipped shim the gating probe cannot see: `$Config{extensions}`
empty + no `d_getpbyname`), which is the same file seen from the module side.
subject: PCL %Config is a 108-key hand-written subset where perl has 1,253: a missing key makes a file skip_all ITSELF and produce no rows (7 files in the op/ tail; op/lfs.t is 17)
